decision_reason: Iteration 1 surfaced strong candidate sources across all four target source types (official Brazilian MoH/SVS bulletin on gov.br, PAHO situation report dated March 28 2024, state-level bulletins from Minas Gerais and Distrito Federal, InfoDengue platform, and Brazilian news outlets). However, the snippets confirm that the gov.br boletim result references SE 4 (early February 2024) and the PAHO result is dated March 28 2024 — both within the Q1 2024 window — but the metadata does not confirm full coverage of SE 1–13 (Jan 1–Mar 31). Key gaps remain: (1) No SVS bulletin explicitly covering the end of Q1 (SE 10–13, i.e., March 2024) was surfaced; the gov.br result appears to be Boletim Vol. 55 No. 11, which may cover a later period. (2) No state-level subnational breakdown with confirmed/probable/suspected/deaths disaggregated by UF for the full Q1 window was confirmed in snippets. (3) The national emergency declaration (February 2024) document was not surfaced. (4) The PAHO March 28 alert references Brazil's share of Americas cases (83%) but does not provide Q1-specific Brazil case totals in the snippet. (5) ReliefWeb results (2 hits) were not summarized — these may contain WHO/PAHO situation reports with Q1-specific data. A second iteration with 4 targeted queries can close these gaps: (a) a direct SVS/saude.gov.br search for the specific Q1 2024 dengue monitoring panel or emergency declaration, (b) a PAHO epidemiological alert search specifically for the February 2024 Brazil emergency, (c) a ReliefWeb-targeted search for Brazil dengue Q1 2024 situation reports, and (d) a state-level subnational search targeting high-burden states (São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro) for Q1 2024 data. This is iteration 2 of 2 (max), so this is the final query batch.
coverage_assessment: Partial. Iteration 1 confirmed: (1) One SVS boletim epidemiológico on gov.br with SE 4 data (260k probable cases, 29 deaths); (2) PAHO March 28 2024 alert with Brazil share of Americas cases; (3) State-level bulletin pages for Minas Gerais and Distrito Federal; (4) InfoDengue platform homepage; (5) Brazilian news (Folha, Agência Brasil, G1) and Cofen article with full-year 2024 totals. Missing: explicit Q1 cumulative totals (SE 1–13) at national level with confirmed/probable/suspected/deaths breakdown; national emergency declaration document; subnational (UF-level) case breakdown for Q1; PAHO or WHO situation report with Brazil-specific Q1 case counts; ReliefWeb situation reports not yet summarized.
source_diversity_assessment: Good diversity across source types: official Brazilian federal (gov.br), official Brazilian state (saude.mg.gov.br, saude.df.gov.br), international organization (paho.org, who.int), structured database (info.dengue.mat.br), academic (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), news (folha, agenciabrasil, g1), and humanitarian aggregator (reliefweb.int). YouTube results (4 hits) are low-value for structured data extraction. Academic/preprint sources (researchgate, researchsquare, scielo, medcraveonline) may contain Q1-specific data but are secondary. The gov.br and paho.org hits are the highest-value candidates. ReliefWeb (2 hits) not yet summarized — may contain additional PAHO/WHO situation reports.
trustworthiness_assessment: High for gov.br (SVS boletim epidemiológico — primary authoritative source), paho.org (international organization — cross-validator), saude.mg.gov.br and saude.df.gov.br (state health secretariats — authoritative for subnational data). Moderate for agenciabrasil.ebc.com.br (official Brazilian government news agency — cites MoH data), g1.globo.com and folha.uol.com.br (major Brazilian news — typically cite official figures). Low for YouTube (not extractable as structured data), cofen.gov.br (nursing council — secondary aggregator), ghc.com.br (hospital group — facility-level, not population-level). Academic sources (PMC, SciELO) are peer-reviewed but may not provide Q1-specific granularity.
disease_location_time_fit_assessment: Disease fit: Strong — all top results are dengue-specific. Location fit: Strong — Brazil is the primary location in all top results. Time fit: Partial — the gov.br boletim snippet references SE 4 (late January/early February 2024), within Q1; the PAHO alert is dated March 28 2024, within Q1; the Cofen article references full-year 2024 totals (through October), which extends beyond Q1 but may contain Q1 sub-period data; the GHC informe references 2024–2025 data, partially out of scope. The MG and DF state bulletins reference dates (22/06) that appear to be June 2024, outside Q1 — these may be index pages for bulletin archives that include Q1 editions. InfoDengue homepage is undated. Need to confirm Q1-specific data in a second iteration.
corroboration_potential_assessment: The gov.br SVS boletim and PAHO March 28 alert are mutually corroborating at the national level. State bulletins (MG, DF) corroborate subnational data. InfoDengue can corroborate municipality-level data. Brazilian news outlets (Agência Brasil, G1, Folha) typically cite MoH figures directly and can corroborate national totals. A second iteration targeting the national emergency declaration and additional PAHO/WHO situation reports will strengthen corroboration for the Q1 cumulative totals and deaths fields.
